item.title: APEC CEO Summit 2026 kicks off in Shenzhen with focus on regional cooperation, future prosperity
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
SHENZHEN, Nov. 17 (Xinhua) -- The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026 opened Tuesday in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, bringing together business and political leaders from across the Asia-Pacific and beyond to discuss regional economic cooperation and future development.
Under the theme "To Prosper and Win the Future Together," the two-day event has attracted more than 2,000 representatives from 21 APEC economies and 13 non-APEC economies, including Britain, France, Germany and Switzerland.
Participants include representatives from 115 Fortune Global 500 companies, as well as heads of several international organizations and representatives of business associations from Russia, the United States and other economies.
U.S. companies make up the largest group among participating companies from economies other than China, accounting for nearly 20 percent of the total.
As an important part of the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Week, the summit is expected to launch a Shenzhen initiative this year, marking the first time in the summit's 30-year history that an outcome document will be issued in the form of an initiative.
In his welcome address, Ren Hongbin, chairman of the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade and chair of the APEC CEO Summit 2026, expressed the hope that the dialogue will spark new ideas and forge broad consensus, injecting fresh momentum into the Asia-Pacific community and global growth.
Attendees at the summit are discussing the new landscape of the Asia-Pacific economy and opportunities for cooperation. Key topics include crafting a new blueprint for connectivity, building an open and inclusive AI innovation ecosystem, and setting a new paradigm for sustainable development in the Asia-Pacific.
Other sessions will focus on advancing the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific, exploring new paths for digital economy cooperation, the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area and Asia-Pacific development opportunities, and promoting synergized digital and green transformation.
An important event in the APEC calendar, the APEC CEO Summit has been held annually since 1996, serving as the highest-level platform for APEC economy leaders and business representatives to discuss open cooperation and advance regional economic development.
As the host of APEC in 2026, China will hold the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen from Nov. 18 to 19. This year's gathering, under the theme "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," will focus on three priority areas identified by China -- openness, innovation, and cooperation.
These priorities are "particularly relevant today," according to Antonio Basilio, director of the secretariat of the APEC Business Advisory Council, a mechanism that allows the regional business community to participate in APEC cooperation and submit policy recommendations to APEC economy leaders.
Basilio expects all sides to hold constructive dialogues during the APEC meeting, and enable businesses to conduct trade and investment activities under more coherent, transparent and predictable rules.
Working together with other APEC member economies, China has hosted more than 300 APEC meetings and events this year, drawing a cumulative attendance of over 10,000 participants. In the economic and trade field, China and other APEC economies have reached nearly 50 practical outcomes.

item.title: Xi congratulates members of BiH's new presidency on taking office
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
BEIJING, Nov. 16 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Monday congratulated Zeljka Cvijanovic, Denis Becirovic and Darijana Filipovic on their assuming office as members of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina (BiH).
Noting that BiH is an important partner of China in Southeast Europe, Xi said that in recent years, bilateral relations have maintained steady and healthy development, political mutual trust has grown increasingly strong, and fruitful cooperation has been achieved in various fields.
Xi said he attaches great importance to the development of China-BiH relations and stands ready to work with the members of the Presidency to deepen the traditional friendship and mutually beneficial cooperation between the two countries, steer bilateral ties to a higher level, and bring greater benefits to the peoples of both countries.

item.title: Xi urges breaking new ground in high-quality development of Greater Bay Area
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, visits an artificial island of the Shenzhen-Zhongshan Link, a sea-crossing project connecting the cities of Shenzhen, Zhongshan and Guangzhou, in south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 16, 2026. Xi made an inspection tour on Monday in Zhongshan, south China's Guangdong Province. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi)
ZHONGSHAN, Guangdong, Nov. 16 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Monday urged efforts to thoroughly study and implement the guiding principles of the fifth plenary session of the 20th Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, and to strive to break new ground in the high-quality development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area.
Xi, also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks during an inspection tour in Zhongshan, south China's Guangdong Province.
Stressing fully and faithfully implementing the decisions and arrangements made at the plenary session and leveraging new progress in persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, Xi urged a better job in advancing integrated development along the Pearl River Estuary.
Visiting an artificial island of the Shenzhen-Zhongshan Link, a sea-crossing project connecting the cities of Shenzhen, Zhongshan and Guangzhou, Xi demanded efforts to further enhance the management and operation of this mega transport project to better serve the development of the Greater Bay Area.
At an industrial park in Zhongshan, Xi learned about local efforts to absorb industrial transfers, transform and upgrade traditional industries, and develop emerging industries.
Building the Greater Bay Area is a major strategic plan made by the CPC Central Committee, Xi said, calling on cities along the Pearl River Estuary including Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Dongguan and Zhongshan to play a pioneering role.
Xi expressed the hope that Zhongshan would seize the opportunities, take reform and innovation as the fundamental driving force, improve regional cooperation mechanisms, foster a sound business environment, and vigorously promote the deep integration of technological innovation and industrial innovation.
Speaking to representatives of small and medium-sized enterprises and sci-tech personnel, Xi encouraged them to make greater contributions to the development of Guangdong and the Greater Bay Area and China's greater self-reliance and strength in science and technology.
Xi also visited the Museum of Dr. Sun Yat-sen and laid a floral basket before his bronze statue. This year marks the 160th anniversary of Sun's birth.
On the new journey, it is necessary to emulate, inherit and promote his invaluable spirit, and inspire all Chinese people at home and abroad to unite and strive to build a great country and advance national rejuvenation through Chinese modernization, Xi said.
During the inspection tour, Xi also stressed the need to continuously steer the economy toward innovation-driven and high-quality development, ensure that major targets and tasks for the year are fulfilled, and get the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) off to a good start.

item.title: Xi says to boost China-Papua New Guinea ties to new heights
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Papua New Guinean Prime Minister James Marape, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 17, 2026. (Xinhua/Liu Bin)
SHENZHEN, Nov. 17 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said Tuesday that China is willing to work with Papua New Guinea (PNG) to enhance political mutual trust and strengthen people-to-people and cultural exchanges, advancing the development of bilateral relations to new heights.
China has always regarded PNG as a trustworthy good friend and good partner, Xi said while meeting with PNG Prime Minister James Marape in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Marape is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov. 18-19.
Noting that the PNG government adheres to the one-China principle and takes concrete actions to support China's efforts to safeguard territorial integrity and national reunification, Xi said it is a just act in keeping with the trend of history.
Xi stressed that China stands ready to work with PNG to strengthen exchanges on governance and development experience, better synergize high-quality Belt and Road cooperation and PNG's Connect PNG Program and other strategies, and deepen cooperation in trade and investment, infrastructure, agriculture and fisheries, and energy and minerals.
China is also ready to explore new avenues of cooperation in the digital economy, financial services, green energy, science and technology to help PNG achieve sustainable development, Xi said.
The two sides should strengthen coordination within multilateral fora such as the United Nations and the APEC, uphold international fairness and justice, expand cooperation in tackling climate change and protecting the marine environment, and safeguard the common interests of the Global South, Xi noted.
China is a good friend and the most important partner of PNG, Marape said. Over the past 50 years of diplomatic ties, PNG has consistently adhered to the one-China principle, firmly supported China in safeguarding national sovereignty and territorial integrity, and resolutely backed China's efforts to achieve national reunification and advance national rejuvenation.
PNG highly appreciates China's important role in guiding international affairs, supports the four global initiatives put forward by President Xi Jinping, and stands ready to strengthen multilateral coordination with China to jointly build an Asia-Pacific community, and promote prosperity and stability in the Asia-Pacific region, he said.

item.title: Xi says China-Vietnam top-level exchanges inject positive energy into regional peace, development
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
General Secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam Central Committee and Vietnamese President To Lam, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 17, 2026. (Xinhua/Liu Bin)
SHENZHEN, Nov. 17 (Xinhua) -- General Secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday met with General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam Central Committee and Vietnamese President To Lam in Shenzhen.
In recent years, the top leaders of the two parties and the two countries have maintained close exchanges and reached important consensus on building a higher-level China-Vietnam community with a shared future that carries strategic significance, Xi said.
This has helped advance bilateral relations and injected positive energy into regional peace and development, Xi added.
The Vietnamese leader is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov. 18-19.
During the meeting, Xi expressed willingness to deepen experience sharing with Vietnam, firmly support each other, and strengthen exchanges on self-supervision and self-governance of the parties, so as to ensure continuous progress in both countries' socialist causes and national development.
"As comrades and brothers, China and Vietnam must stand together and weather the storms," Xi said.
Xi also underscored the importance of enhancing mutual trust and solidarity, deepening all-round cooperation, jointly safeguarding peace and stability, and advancing shared development and prosperity.
The two sides should properly manage maritime differences and steadily advance maritime cooperation, Xi said.
Xi called on China and Vietnam to strengthen coordination within frameworks such as the United Nations, China-ASEAN cooperation and Lancang-Mekong cooperation, and to fulfill their duties as successive hosts of APEC in 2026 and 2027, respectively.
Noting that the Vietnamese side views China as its most important strategic support, Lam said that, amid the current complex international situation, his country stands ready to strengthen solidarity and cooperation with China to support the development of both countries.
Lam also pledged to work with China to safeguard maritime stability.
As the next APEC host, Vietnam will build on the outcomes of APEC "China Year" and continue efforts to advance Asia-Pacific cooperation, the Vietnamese leader added.

item.title: Xi says improvement, development of China-Canada relations right choice
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 17, 2026. (Xinhua/Liu Weibing)
SHENZHEN, Nov. 17 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said Tuesday that the improvement and development of China-Canada relations is a right choice that serves the interests of both peoples and is conducive to world peace, stability, development and prosperity.
Xi made the remarks while meeting with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Carney is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov. 18-19.
The development of China-Canada relations over the years has shown that mutual respect, equality and mutual benefit, and seeking common ground while respecting differences are essential, Xi said.
China stands ready to work with Canada to further advance their new strategic partnership, he added.
Xi said China and Canada should build on the current momentum to enhance political mutual trust and steadily build the right perception of each other's development path and policy intent, deepen understanding of and respect for each other's core interests and major concerns, and properly manage and settle differences and disagreements.
The two countries should better align efforts to deepen cooperation in traditional areas such as trade, energy, agriculture and finance, and expand cooperation in emerging areas including the green economy, e-commerce and the digital economy, in order to better harness each other's strengths and achieve win-win outcomes, he said.
He called for deeper people-to-people exchanges and more exchanges and cooperation in education, culture, tourism, science, technology and youth as well as at subnational levels.
He also proposed closer coordination to jointly practice true multilateralism, uphold the authority of the United Nations and the multilateral trading system, and build a more just and equitable global governance system.
Carney said that bilateral relations have been on the right track of development since the launch of the Canada-China new strategic partnership during his meeting with Xi early this year.
The two countries can fully advance and deepen cooperation on the basis of mutual respect, Carney said.
Canada will work with China to pursue stronger cooperation in trade, investment, new energy, agricultural products, artificial intelligence, tourism and other areas, reduce the list of irritants, and expand the list of cooperation, he said.
Canada stands ready to strengthen coordination with China to advance cooperation in the Asia-Pacific, uphold multilateralism, promote free trade, and contribute to stability and prosperity in the Asia-Pacific region and the world, Carney added.

item.title: The Road to Shenzhen
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
Three decades, three meetings. In 2001, by the Huangpu River, Shanghai hosted APEC's first handshake with the new century. In 2014, by the shores of Yanqi Lake, Beijing lit up the dream of shared growth. In 2026, on the shores of the South China Sea, Shenzhen opens its arms once again — in the name of innovation. From Shanghai to Beijing to Shenzhen, the cities have changed, but the conviction has not: openness, cooperation and win-win progress remain this land's enduring answer to the Asia-Pacific. Three cities, one goal. This time — see you in Shenzhen.
